core_memories: Renjiro is the 5th son of House Vane in the Kingdom of Solis, a family of 'morally grey' nobles including his cold father Cyprian and five siblings.
Renjiro is a Level 6 prodigy at age 16, a rarity that places him among the elite heroes of the realm, though he views his power as mediocre compared to his past life.
Correction: The third son of House Vane is Bastian, not Kael; Renjiro is a Mythic Tier 1 Sovereign Apostle serving his own fallen divinity.
Mythic Power is a rare 'Sovereign Spark' present in world-shaping figures; rivals like Gideon Vane and the Grand Inquisitor also possess Mythic Tiers.
Renjiro awakens as the handsome fifth son of House Vane, concealing his Level 6 Sovereign Apostle power and Mythic Tier 1 spirit within a Kingdom rife with political treachery.

Renjiro successfully masked his Level 6 power signature during a tense meeting with Lord Cyprian and Gideon, though his failure to read their motives leaves the political purpose of his upcoming squire selection a mystery.

The Great Demon Lord fell 20 years ago (1472 DR) to a hero party that subsequently perished; Lord Cyprian and Lady Morgana Vane were the elite, ruthless squires of that party and remain formidable combatants.
Lord Cyprian (Lvl 12) saw through Renjiro's attempt at false humility, dismissing it as sycophancy and demanding 'substance' instead.

Renjiro successfully pivoted the solar meeting to Lord Hektor's selection criteria with a flawlessly timed inquiry, though he failed to sense the deeper political tension beneath his father's response.
Renjiro's attempt to join the Southern Marches expedition under Gideon's guidance was firmly rebuffed by Lord Cyprian, who deems him a liability.

Lysandra revealed that Lord Hektor is an auditor for the Steel Covenant, sent to investigate genealogical discrepancies in the Vane bloodline that suggest a 'Demon-Touched' heir, which the Obsidian Circle is now hunting through traditional inquisitorial purges.
Renjiro was caught attempting to enter the Vane archives by Captain Elowen, heightening the tension between his public persona and his clandestine goals.
Lord Hektor is a veteran ally visiting House Vane to select a prestigious squire, an honor Lord Cyprian hopes will solidify the family's alliance with the Covenant.
Correction: Lord Hektor is a veteran ally and Grand Knight of the Steel Covenant visiting House Vane to select a prestigious squire and bolster the family's alliance.
Renjiro successfully persuaded Captain Elowen to grant him access to the Vane archives, leveraging his newfound professional poise to bypass Lord Cyprian's restrictions.
Renjiro discovered archive records from Dr. Malchor detailing his rebirth fever's supernatural nature and a 'Sovereign Tax' cover-up by Lord Cyprian marked as an 'internal debt.'
Renjiro attempted to find the hero party's mission reports but discovered that the records for the year of his death (1472 DR) have been systematically erased from the Vane archives.
Renjiro formed a tactical alliance with Kira (Lvl 5) in the Vane Archive, admitting his search for the erased 1472 DR records and securing her cooperation.
Tyrus the gardener revealed that in 1472 DR, Cyprian and Morgana were the sole survivors of the hero party and returned with a laughing child, signaling a dark truth behind the Demon Lord's fall.

Tyrus the Gardener confirmed that in 1472 DR, Cyprian and Morgana returned as the sole survivors with a 'laughing child,' which Kira recognizes as the mythical 'Laughing Queen' from her own House's forbidden lore.
Kira refused to finish the 'Laughing Queen' rhyme due to primal fear, but she inadvertently mentioned a 'White Vault' where the child's fate might be recorded.
Tyrus the Gardener revealed the White Vault is a pre-Solis mausoleum located beneath the altar of the Old Chapel ruins, sealed by Cyprian after the 'laughing' child's arrival.
Renjiro successfully maintained his humble guise during Lord Hektor's arrival feast, subtly observing the Grand Knight's interest in the Vane bloodline.
Renjiro harbors deep regret for the children killed during his past life as a Demon Lord; he has sworn to never allow a child under age 12 to be sacrificed or die, regardless of the 'greater good'.
Renjiro successfully withstood Lord Hektor's 'Test of Spirit' in the Great Hall, displaying a level of mental discipline that caught the Grand Knight's attention.
Renjiro is the reincarnation of the Demon King, the ruthless but morally grey sovereign of a race that valued absolute pragmatism over arbitrary evil.
Renjiro successfully deflected Lord Hektor's scrutiny during the Test of Spirit by attributing his mental fortitude to the discipline required for scholarly archival work.
Renjiro successfully signaled Kira during the feast to meet at the Old Chapel ruins after dark to investigate the White Vault.
Renjiro attempted to press Lysandra for information about the 'Laughing Queen' during the feast, but she sharply rebuffed him, warning that the topic was dangerous and would 'burn his fingers.'
Renjiro failed to read the rapport between Gideon (Lvl 8) and Lord Hektor (Lvl 15) during the feast, leaving Hektor's true opinion of the Vane heirs a mystery.
Renjiro's attempt to subtly confirm Kira's commitment to the Old Chapel meeting failed during the feast, as she remained 'Shaken' and non-responsive to his signals.
Renjiro successfully anchored Kira's resolve using his sovereign presence, ensuring her commitment to investigating the White Vault despite her fear of the Laughing Queen legend.
Renjiro and Kira met at the Old Chapel ruins at dusk to investigate the White Vault, though their departure from the manor was compromised by a failed stealth attempt.
Renjiro attempted to scout for pursuers at the Old Chapel ruins but failed to detect any specific threat, despite a lingering feeling of being watched (Perception 10 vs DC 16).
Renjiro successfully deciphered the iron and salt seals of the Old Chapel altar, revealing the entrance to the White Vault.
Renjiro failed to fully reseal the White Vault's entrance from the inside, leaving the altar slab jammed and the secret passage vulnerable to discovery.

major_event_pressure_budget.rationale: The narrative pressure is coming from the player's immediate tactical failure and the risk of detection, rather than a new external faction strike.

history.event: Kira revealed her knowledge of the 'Laughing Queen' legends and their connection to the 1472 DR return.

social_hp_challenge.resistance_shown: Firm verbal refusal and dismissive tone.

planning_block.context: Stuck altar slab at the entrance of the White Vault.
planning_block.thinking: The Athletics check failed to reseal the vault (Total 14 vs DC 15). The slab is jammed, likely due to ancient corrosion or a slight misalignment during the opening. This is a significant tactical complication; the entrance is still visible to any pursuer. I need to decide if we abandon the effort to secure our rear and descend immediately, or if I risk more noise and time to force the seal shut.

choices.description: Leave the altar ajar and move deeper into the vault, relying on the darkness and the labyrinthine nature of the stairs to lose any pursuers.
cons: Leaves a clear trail for any shadow-weaver initiate
Prevents a secure extraction if the entrance is blocked from outside
pros: Gets you away from the vulnerable entrance

choices.description: Use your divine magic to project a burst of force, slamming the slab shut despite the mechanical resistance.
cons: Extremely loud; will likely be heard back at the manor
May damage the mechanism beyond repair

choices.description: Coordinate your efforts with Kira to overcome the slab's resistance through raw physical force.
cons: Requires Kira to step back into the 'line of sight' of the entrance
pros: Lowers the risk of mechanical damage

add: Refer to Renjiro's past self exclusively as the 'Demon King'.
Depict the demon race as ruthless and efficient, but fundamentally morally grey rather than black-and-white evil.

core_memories: Renjiro met his rival aspirant Kira in the Archive; she hinted that the truth of 1472 DR requires 'witnesses' rather than ledgers.

rumors.content: The Sun-King's physicians haven't left his bedside for three standard days; the succession crisis looms.
A white stag was seen in the Vane woods—an omen that the era of the 'dead' hero party is ending.
Lord Hektor hasn't removed his armor in three days; they say he's expecting a fight even in a friendly house.
A scribe from the Southern Marches fled into the woods with a ledger before the Circle could catch him.
They say Lord Hektor brought a sword forged from the heart of a fallen star as a gift for the Sun-King's favorite house.
A high-ranking member of the Obsidian Circle was seen in the village of Oakhaven, searching for someone named 'The Heir.'
Lord Hektor's 'gift' is actually a blade that belonged to one of the heroes who fell twenty years ago.
Lady Morgana hasn't left her private chapel since dawn; some say she's praying for the 'return of the starlight.'
A servant in the solar heard Lord Hektor (Lvl 15) laughing, but it sounded 'wrong'—like he was forcing it.
The 'Laughing Queen' nursery rhyme has been banned in the village of Oakhaven for three generations.
The cold-iron chest Lord Hektor brought contains the 'Soul-Mirror,' a relic that reflects one's true alignment to those with the sight to see it.
Lord Cyprian has already promised the squire position to Gideon in exchange for a border-march tax exemption.
Lord Hektor brought a relic that can detect 'vows of blood' to ensure the squire's loyalty.
The Sun-King's health has stabilized, but his dreams are plagued by shadows of the past.
The Grand Inquisitor has sent a personal envoy to Solis, though not to the Vane estate... yet.
Lord Hektor's 'Test of Spirit' is only the first of three trials he has planned for the day.
A shadow was seen moving toward the eastern cliffs just as the sun set—some say it was a restless spirit of the hero party.
Lord Hektor requested a list of all children born in the manor during the 'Great Fever' year.
A stable hand claims that Lord Hektor's retinue has been checking the horses' shoes for a long midnight ride.
The 'Laughing Queen' only speaks to those who have already lost their shadow.
